stranglerCase.title: Strangler Fig Migration Demo
stranglerCase.summary: A public technical study of incrementally migrating a legacy PHP/Yii read path to Node.js + Next.js while keeping the public URL stable through nginx.
stranglerCase.visualsTitle: The behavior gap becomes visible in the interface itself
stranglerCase.visualsSubtitle: Instead of relying only on architecture diagrams, the study shows the contrast between legacy polling, the modern stream, and canonical-route cutover in a public interface.

visuals.title: Direct comparison between legacy and modern paths
visuals.description: The same business action exposes the delay of the legacy snapshot and the immediate response of the modern stream in the same dashboard.
visuals.alt: Dashboard screenshot comparing the legacy PHP panel with the modern real-time panel.

visuals.title: Live cutover while keeping the same public URL
visuals.description: The gateway keeps the canonical route stable while switching the upstream between legacy and modern to demonstrate the strangler strategy.
visuals.alt: Dashboard screenshot showing the live cutover block with the same public route served by different upstreams.

stranglerCase.statusValue: Public PoC with live demo and open repository

facts.label: Goal
facts.value: Show incremental migration without changing the public URL

facts.label: Legacy path
facts.value: PHP/Yii with synchronous polling and artificial delay

facts.label: Modern path
facts.value: Node.js + Socket.IO + Next.js in real time

facts.label: Gateway
facts.value: nginx with reversible cutover between upstreams

proofItems: Legacy and modern stack coexist behind the same public contract
Canonical route cutover stays reversible without breaking the client URL
The UX gain becomes visible when synchronous polling gives way to real-time events
stranglerCase.overviewBody: The goal was to make a common modernization story visible: a legacy PHP/Yii controller still serves business data through polling, while a modern Node.js implementation publishes the same event immediately. Instead of talking about architecture in the abstract, the demo shows the behavioral gap side by side.
stranglerCase.problemBody: Full rewrites are expensive and risky when the public route is already in use. This study starts from that scenario: keep the canonical URL stable, preserve coexistence between implementations, and allow the read path to move gradually.
technical: Next.js dashboard comparing the legacy snapshot with the modern stream
Node.js/TypeScript service with Socket.IO, Postgres, and Redis
Legacy PHP/Yii layer with HTTP polling, MySQL, and simulated latency
nginx gateway handling the canonical route and live cutover
operations: The public URL remains the same throughout the migration
The gateway decides which upstream serves the canonical route
The same business event feeds both read paths
Cutover can move forward to modern or back to legacy with low friction
stranglerCase.ctaTitle: See the live demo and the repository
stranglerCase.ctaBody: This study is useful for conversations about incremental modernization, PHP legacy systems, reverse-proxy gateways, and a safer transition into a Node.js/Next.js stack.
